title: Dimensionality Reduction: PCA and t-SNE
description: How PCA and t-SNE compress high-dimensional data into fewer dimensions - one by capturing maximum variance, the other by preserving local structure for visualization.
content:
**Dimensionality reduction** is a technique used to reduce the number of features (i.e. dimensions) in the input data while preserving as much information as possible.

**Principal Component Analysis (PCA)** identifies the directions - the principal components - that capture the maximum variance in the data.

How PCA works:
• The principal components are orthogonal, which means they are uncorrelated with each other.
• The first component captures the most variance, followed by the second, the third and so on.
• Mathematically, PCA involves calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of the input data.
• The algorithm then projects the data onto the low-dimensional space formed by the principal components.

**t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding (t-SNE)** focuses on preserving the local structure of data points. Its core idea is that similar data points in high-dimensional space should be represented as nearby points in the low-dimensional space, and vice versa.

How t-SNE works:
• It calculates similarities between points via a t-distribution.
• It minimizes the divergence between the distributions of pairwise similarities in the low-dimensional space.

**PCA vs. t-SNE at a glance:**
• PCA is a linear technique, while t-SNE is non-linear.
• PCA is commonly used in feature engineering and data preprocessing, and is considered computationally effective compared to t-SNE.
• t-SNE is effective for exploratory data analysis and for visualizing high-dimensional clusters or manifolds in a low-dimensional space.
